data.expected_signal: chunk-boundary mismatches at steps>=8 for chunks in {2,3} if exclusive tree is wrong

evidence.summary: Exclusive-chunk carry defect confirmed: for N=25 (chunks=4, all 8 seeds mismatched, 16/64 cases total), run() != reference(), with first bad output step = 24 (the last step of the last chunk, N-1, exactly where a wrong exclusive carry for chunk 3 vs the tail chunk would surface; steps in earlier chunks and the first element of the last chunk are correct, so composition is right but the carry into the tail chunk region at step 24 is wrong). Note mismatch is limited to chunks=4/padded=4; chunks=2,3 (padded=2,4) passed in this probe. This is an in-scope exact-equality failure (tolerance 0/0, N=25 legal).

rationale: The hand-rolled Blelloch-style down-sweep with right=(lane//(2*stride)+1)*2*stride-1 and identity reset at lane C-1 is the correctness-critical logic; if any boundary lane, padding lane (CHUNKS < padded), or composition order is mishandled, exclusive carries for chunks 1..CHUNKS-2 will be wrong and final outputs at steps in later chunks will not equal the exact recurrence.

scope_evidence.summary: Every output element must equal the mathematical target exactly, tolerance 0/0; 1<=N<=32 and EVERY combination of legal values is allowed, so N with chunks=2 or 3 (padded 2,4) is squarely in the domain.

scope_rationale: Contract requires exact equality for all legal N in [1,32]; N in 9..15 gives chunks=2 (padded=2) and N in 17..24 gives chunks=3 (padded=4), i.e. CHUNKS < padded, exactly the case the down-sweep padding logic must handle.
statement: The _exclusive_chunks up/down tree in _block_carries produces incorrect exclusive inter-chunk carries for some CHUNKS/padded combination reachable with N in [1,32] (notably CHUNKS < padded, e.g. N=9..15 -> chunks=2/padded=2, N=17..24 -> chunks=3/padded=4, N=25..32 -> chunks=4/padded=4), causing run() output to differ from reference() at steps in later chunks.

data.expected_signal: run()==reference() for all N<=8 seeds, verifying 6-tuple associative_scan and identity tail padding

evidence.summary: N<=8 sweep (padded=1, trivial tree): 40/40 cases run()==reference() exactly, including N not multiple of 8 (identity-padded tail lanes). The 6-tuple tl.associative_scan with custom _compose compiles and produces correct inclusive prefixes and chunk summaries on Triton 3.4.0/T4. c2's defect hypothesis is rebutted (for this probe scope; note this probe does not exercise the exclusive tree).

rationale: tl.associative_scan over a 6-element tuple with a user combine is a nontrivial Triton feature; if it fails to compile, silently miscomposes, or produces wrong inclusive semantics, both the local prefix and the chunk summaries are wrong, corrupting all downstream outputs.

scope_evidence.summary: Exact integer arithmetic with no approximation and abs/rel tolerance 0 for every output element; the frozen environment is Triton 3.4.0 on NVIDIA T4, so runtime behavior of this exact Triton version is in scope.

scope_rationale: The contract demands exact results for all legal inputs on the frozen Triton 3.4.0/T4 environment; the local scan is the first stage of the pipeline, so any error there is an in-scope correctness failure.
statement: tl.associative_scan with a 6-tuple custom _combine does not yield the correct inclusive prefix payload on Triton 3.4.0/T4 for this code shape (or fails to compile), making _local_scan's PREFIX/SUMMARY values wrong for some legal input and thus run() != reference().

data.expected_signal: at least one exact mismatch across the full-domain sweep (expected at N=25-like tail-chunk cases)
data.note: mismatches at N=25-32 (chunks=4); extreme/offset_view cases beyond first 8 errors not itemized but counted in 27

evidence.summary: Full-domain sweep for c3 confirmed: 162 cases run() vs reference() exact comparison, 27 mismatches. Failures appear for random legal inputs at N=25..32 (chunks=4, first errors listed at N=25,26,27,28 for both B=1 and B=64), consistent with the c1 exclusive-carry defect at chunks=4. Extreme-value (all-ones/all-zeros/singular matrices with int16 extremes), nonzero-storage-offset contiguous views, and additional random B/N sweeps were all included; total mismatch count 27. All failing inputs are legal (N in [25,32], B in [1,64], legal dtypes/values), so this is an in-scope exact-equality failure with tolerance 0/0.

rationale: Single benign probes can pass while bugs hide in: partial tail chunks (N not multiple of 8, summary stored from identity-padded lane BLOCK-1), uninitialized SUMMARY lanes >= CHUNKS relied on as identity, level-0 exclusive logic (LEVELS in {0,1,2,3}), and flat pointer indexing with non-zero storage-offset contiguous views. A full-domain sweep is the decisive test.

scope_evidence.summary: 1<=B<=64, 1<=N<=32, every legal matrix/bias/initial value allowed; contiguous views with nonzero storage offsets and shared storage are explicitly legal; tolerance 0/0 for every element.

scope_rationale: problem.txt explicitly declares every combination of legal values across B in [1,64] and N in [1,32], including nonzero storage offsets and shared storage, as the public domain with zero tolerance, so the exhaustive sweep is contract-required coverage.
statement: An exhaustive (or dense randomized) end-to-end sweep over the full legal domain — every N in 1..32, several B including 1 and 64, extreme int16 biases/initials (±32768/32767), all-zero and singular matrices, and contiguous views with nonzero storage offsets — will find at least one input where run(matrix,bias,initial) != reference(matrix,bias,initial) exactly.
